How to play “Mercadillo 505 — The Design Review”

The game repeats Class 3 of IT 505 · Fundamentals of Database Technologies in another form: you solve a problem first, and the idea is explained after your attempt. This guide shows every step with a short animation recorded from the game itself. Reading it takes about five minutes; the game takes about twenty-five.

✔ The game is FORMATIVE, not SUMMATIVE. Points, stars and badges give you feedback only. Nothing counts toward your final grade, and nothing leaves your browser.
1OpenDouble-click the game file. It opens in your browser.
2Choose a stationStart with Mission 1; the orange frame marks the next one.
3Problem → Idea → Practice → CheckTry first, read the idea, practise, answer six questions.
4Collect starsThree stars from 90 % of the points. Play again to improve.

1Open the game and read the map

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. Open the file IT505_Class03_GAME.html with a double click. It opens in your browser: Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Nothing is installed, and the game works without an Internet connection.
  2. The first screen says how to play. Click Start playing.
  3. The map shows six stations: four missions (one per lesson of the class), the design review of the studio, and a final round.
  4. The station with the orange frame is the next one. All stations are open, so you can also choose another one.

2Every mission starts with a problem

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. Read the yellow box. It describes a situation in the fictional market Mercadillo 505.
  2. Answer with what you know, before any explanation. A wrong answer costs nothing.
  3. Green means right; red means not yet. In both cases a short note explains why.
  4. Click Next after each item. When all items are done, Continue becomes active.

3Read the idea cards

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. After the problem, the game explains the idea behind it.
  2. Each card has a short explanation on the left and the slide of the lecture on the right. Click the slide to enlarge it; click again, or press Esc, to close it.
  3. Next idea shows the next card. After the last card, Continue opens the practice.

4Practice: draw the marks of a line

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. In Mission 2 you read a business rule and draw it. Choose the minimum (zero or one) and the maximum (one or many) for the highlighted end of the line.
  2. The line is drawn while you choose. Click Check the marks.
  3. The explanation names the marks: circle = zero, bar = one, fork = many.

5Practice: accept or refuse a row

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. In Mission 3 you are the database. Four tables are shown; statements arrive one after the other.
  2. Decide: accept the statement, refuse it because of a primary key, or refuse it because of a foreign key.
  3. An accepted row appears in green in its table. For a refused row you see the real message of the database DuckDB.

6Check: six questions with hints

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. Six questions close each mission. They are formative: they give feedback and do not count toward your grade.
  2. Need a hint? shows a hint before you answer.
  3. A question marked MCQ (Multiple-Choice Question) has one right answer: click it. A question marked MSQ (Multiple-Select Question) has several; their number stands in round brackets. Tick them, then click Check my answer.
  4. After your answer, the note under your choice says why it is right or not right. Show the explanation of every option opens all the reasons.

7Stars, points, levels and badges

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. The result screen shows your stars: one for finishing the station, two from 70 % of its points, three from 90 %.
  2. Points become experience points, written XP (experience points), and experience points become levels, from “Trainee analyst” to “Database architect”.
  3. Each finished station gives a badge. The final round gives its badge from 8 right answers of 10.
  4. Play a station again to improve its stars. Reset my progress, under the map, erases stars, points and badges.

8The library: slides, flashcards, videos, links

The animation repeats. The orange ring shows where to click; the dark line under the picture says what happens.
  1. Library is always in the menu at the top.
  2. Slides with notes: the 55 slides of the lecture. Click a slide to read its key point and its bullet points.
  3. Flashcards: 25 cards. Say the answer aloud, then click the card to turn it.
  4. The other tabs hold the words and abbreviations, the videos (each 15 minutes or shorter), the official links, the summary of the labs and the legal notice.

What the points mean

You do thisYou get
One right decision in a problem or a practice1 point and 5 XP (experience points)
One right answer in the six questions1 point and 10 experience points
Finishing a station for the first time20 experience points and its badge
70 % of the points of a station★★
90 % of the points of a station★★★
150 experience pointsThe next level

The six stations give 18 stars in all. The numbers are for you only.

Good to know

  • Your progress stays in your browser. If you open the game in another browser, on another computer or in a private window, it starts from zero.
  • You cannot break anything. Every station can be played again, and the questions stay the same, so the second round is easier.
  • Keyboard. Tab moves between the buttons, Enter presses one, Esc closes an enlarged slide.
  • Small screen. The game works on a phone; a laptop or a tablet shows the tables more comfortably.
  • Videos and links open in a new tab and need an Internet connection. Check an address before you open it; each one has a link for that.
  • If a page stays empty, the browser blocks JavaScript for local files: allow it for this file, or open the file in another browser.
  • Where the content comes from. Everything in the game is in the student hand-out and in the slides of Class 3; the game adds the practice.
